answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake costly, verifiable proof of unique hardware-backed work before it may transact — like a jade seal that cannot be forged by copying. Reputation then accrues only through attested, non-transferable history, so a flood of mirror copies carries no weight. When a gale of fresh identities arrives, the network throttles unproven accounts until peers vouch for them, making mass fakery expensive while honest newcomers still earn trust.
